question: After the published-package compatibility gap is fixed, should OpenClaw core officially preserve local packaged `dist` mutations and provide opt-in replay after package updates?
rationale: The implementation is technically strong, but supporting modified packaged executable code across updates creates a durable public updater and security contract that code review alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept preservation and replay
options.body: Adopt recovery-bundle preservation by default and the guarded trusted replay flag, with maintained release exceptions.

options.title: Keep recovery only
options.body: Preserve and report local edits but remove automatic replay and its public CLI surface.

options.title: Decline packaged override support
options.body: Keep package installs immutable and direct customization to supported source or plugin paths.

recommendation.title: Accept preservation and replay
recommendation.body: Adopt recovery-bundle preservation by default and the guarded trusted replay flag, with maintained release exceptions.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current updater history, is the live assignee, and is best positioned to decide the core update contract.
